masks-ritual.name: helmet mask
masks-ritual.title: helmet mask
masks-ritual.reason: This is a classic Sowei/Nowo helmet mask with black stained wood, ridged neck rings, and small facial features—a well-documented Sande society masquerade form made and used by the Temne (and related Mende) of Sierra Leone.

masks-ritual.name: bowl
masks-ritual.title: bowl
masks-ritual.reason: A calabash-shell bowl decorated with cowrie shells, bells, bottles and string charms — a medicine man's ritual equipment, plausibly Temne (museum notes "probably"); this is consistent use-object evidence, not decisive attribution but reasonable for the region.

masks-ritual.name: switch
masks-ritual.title: switch
masks-ritual.reason: A cane switch with a cowrie-shell-decorated handle, described as medicine man's equipment attributed to the Temne; such ritual implements are consistent with Temne traditional practice.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: Wooden buffalo/bush-cow mask with raffia fringe, blue pigment, and metal strip, consistent with Temne (Bundu/other society) ritual masks of Sierra Leone; museum records it as Temne-made.

household.name: skyttel
household.title: skyttel
household.reason: A boat-shaped wooden weaving shuttle with thread wound on an internal spindle, collected in Sinkunia, Sierra Leone, a village noted to include Temne among its inhabitants — a plausible everyday tool for the claimed people.

household.name: vävstol, kam, fabric
household.title: vävstol, kam, fabric
household.reason: This is a weaving beater comb (weft beater) from a loom, used to beat weft threads into place during weaving — a textile tool, not a musical instrument, but a plausible Temne-made object from Sierra Leone.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden standing female figure with metal nail eyes and waist binding, consistent with Temne ritual/power figures used in shrine or society contexts.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: Carved wooden female figure with ringed neck, geometric coiffure, and cloth wrap, consistent with Temne nomoli/ancestor-type figures; museum attributes it to Temne (noted as probable). Wooden figurative sculpture used ritually fits the claimed culture.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A wooden standing female figure with separately attached arms and glass-bead earrings, museum-attributed to the Temne — consistent with Temne figural carving traditions used in ritual/society contexts.

sculpture.name: Trästatyett, kvinnofigur
sculpture.title: Trästatyett, kvinnofigur
sculpture.reason: A wooden female figure with disc-topped coiffure and ringed neck, collected in Sierra Leone and attributed to the Temne; carved wood figures of this type are consistent with Temne sculptural traditions.

garment.name: apron
garment.title: apron
garment.reason: A beaded apron with geometric triangle pattern, attributed to the Temne of Sierra Leone by the museum; this is a plausible traditional garment/adornment piece for the region.

garment.name: hatt, hat
garment.title: hatt, hat
garment.reason: A conical woven bast-fiber hat with black-and-yellow geometric overstitching, collected in Sierra Leone and explicitly noted as worn by the Temne (more so than Mende). This is a documented headwear type used by the Temne.

textile.name: Doek
textile.title: Doek
textile.reason: A brown/green batik-dyed cotton cloth made by Kadiato Kamara's son John in Sierra Leone, depicting drummers and a dancer, with a white embroidered border — a traditional textile craft attributed to a named Sierra Leonean (likely Temne) maker.
